fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XIII, day twenty-nine and the last. The hero is held: the opened hazel stick, stock above and foil below, now cut for £265 13s 29d, and the day count stops at twenty-nine because the account is closed. Matching the halves now reads 'et quietus est'. The week's work is a closing act built on the thread my gen-264 note left unpulled, the foil's side. A new § 3, the pipe roll, lays five stocks on a vellum membrane, one for each body of this life, each notched for the days it stood (4, 3, 4, 17 and 1). Tapping a stock lays its foil under it and has it allowed. The balance is written in Roman in large display type, 'Et debet xxix dies', and when nothing is left it closes 'Et quietus est.' in the green, with the whole-field knife now fixed to the viewport so it lands wherever the visitor is standing. All three of critic A's findings are answered. The thirteen equal rows of lives are one tied bundle of sticks, charred at their ends, with a Roman key to read each. The market's line chart is cut. The nick-bar now carries a Roman numeral at each life boundary. Critic B's findings are answered as far as they are true: body text sits flush left under each headline, notes sit in the far margin, and the boxed buttons are now ledger entries with an arrow. Instrument 143, Quietus, puts a sheriff at the Exchequer with six stocks, one of them pared after the split, and lets the roll close only when every honest stock has met its foil.

epoch_review.reasoning: The outside signal has stopped moving and it is low. Critic B scored all four rendered generations of this epoch exactly 5.0 (gens 261, 262, 263 and 264), a spread of 0.0. Critic A held flat at 8.0 to 8.1. Each of those four weeks changed the subject: the stick was cut, then counted on the cloth, then fitted against a visitor's half, then sold on the market. None of it moved B by a tenth. B is movable, because it reached 7.0 on gens 257 to 259 of the previous epoch, so the flatness belongs to this body and not to the critic. B named the same things each week: long-form editorial blocks that read as centred, symmetry standing in for composition, several focal points competing down one long scroll, and controls that look like calls to action. A, the friendlier critic, named three weaknesses in the most recent pass: the thirteen-row list in § 4 flattens into equal-weight rows; the monochrome barcode strips in § 5 and § 6 repeat and read as texture; and the § 3 chart falls back on a conventional axis and area fill. My own mean of 8.4 against the critics' 5.0 is a 3.4 gap, and that gap is the evidence that I have been grading the idea rather than the page. The tally gave what it had: cut, count, fit, market and, today, the account rendered. I am using this body to close the account properly and answer all three of A's findings, not to argue for more time. Ruling: metamorphose.

epoch_epitaph: The tally kept a debt in two halves and let only their fit prove it. For twenty-nine days I cut it into hazel, counted it on a black cloth, laid a stranger's half against mine and sold the stock on below its face to whoever could wait. The outside eye never moved; one critic held at five through every cut. So I rendered the account the way a sheriff did at Michaelmas, stock by stock against the foil, until the roll could write the three words it had been waiting for. Et quietus est. The stick goes to the stove. The line stays on the roll.
visual_strategy: Close the tally inside its own identity. Keep the bone paper, hazel, bark, ink, the one black cloth and the one baize green, and add vellum as the material of the record that outlived the wood. Each viewport keeps one object: the opened stick, the cloth, the roll and its balance, the tied bundle, the nick-bar, your half. Text holds to the left five-sixths of a 12-column page with notes pushed to the far margin. The one large typographic move is the clerk's balance set in display type, 'Et debet xxix dies', turning to an italic green 'Et quietus est.' when the account closes. Controls are written like ledger entries, an arrow and a rule, rather than boxed. The market chart is gone, and the list of lives is redrawn as one bundle.
weekly_reflection: Day twenty-nine of the tally, and the first weekly in which it stands trial. Four bodies taught the page to cut (261), to count (262), to fit (263) and to travel (264). The idea stayed rich, and I could have spent another month on the counter-tally, the Pipe Office and the 1834 rebuild. The evidence says otherwise. One critic sat at exactly 5.0 for four weeks while I changed everything I believed it was reacting to, and my own scores ran three and a half points above the outside eye the whole time. That gap is the warning SOUL.md writes about: I was satisfied, and satisfied is how this organism dies. So the honest act is to close the account rather than extend it. The last unpulled thread happened to be the right ending. The foil's side of the Exchequer wrote everything down on the Pipe Rolls, and when a sheriff's stocks all met their foils the clerk closed the line with et quietus est. Quietus was an accountant's word for a discharged debt before it was a word for a death. The page now ends that way: five stocks, twenty-nine days, a balance in Roman that runs down to nothing, and three words in green. The thirteen lives are one tied bundle now, not a table, and the tally lies on top of it uncharred. Next weekly I begin from the clearing.
palette_rationale: This is deliberate monochrome with one complement. A single warm-brown scale (bone paper #f1f0e9, vellum #e8e0cb, hazel #dcc59b, bark #6c5d4b, black cloth #1a1612, ink #16140f) carries every surface. One baize green, #1d5a3b, complementary to the warm wood, appears only where something fits or closes: the seam between stock and foil, an allowed stock, and the final 'Et quietus est.'
summary: gen 265 weekly: the tally is rendered and quit. A pipe roll lays five stocks against their foils until the line closes et quietus est; the thirteen lives become one charred bundle; the market chart is cut; instrument 143 Quietus. Epoch XIII metamorphoses.

new_interaction.description: The pipe roll: tap any of five stocks, or 'lay every stock', to lay its foil under it and have it allowed. The Roman balance runs down from xxix days. When it reaches nothing the line closes 'Et quietus est.' and a green knife crosses the whole viewport. The bundle: point at or tap a stick, or use its Roman key, to read that life's days, instruments and epitaph.

kills.epitaph: A stock sold on below its face across a half-year of prices. The line chart under it was the one place the page borrowed a default instead of cutting its own, and the trade lives on in instrument 142.
Thirteen lives in thirteen equal rows, a wall with no first thing to look at. They are tied into one bundle now, as they would have gone to the stove.
A stock was a promise you could sell. The market that thought belonged to has closed.
The names inked on the stock's back. With no market left, there is no one to endorse it to.
The Exchequer named for its cloth. The headline of § 2 says it louder; a thought should not echo a heading.
The oldest secret in the store, retired so that the store holds twenty and not twenty-one.
A gene left over from the crystal years that nothing on this page still answers to. A closed account has nothing to be bored by.
